limitations_and_boundaries: Dataset limited to human single-cell transcriptomes; applicability to other species or bulk data not evaluated.
Fine-tuning hyperparameters were fixed across tasks, potentially underestimating maximum predictive potential.
In silico perturbations are computational predictions and require experimental validation.
Pretraining corpus may include task-specific datasets; claim that this does not affect classification predictions is supported by Extended Data Fig. 1f.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

research_questions.statement: Can a context-aware, attention-based deep learning model pretrained on large-scale single-cell transcriptomic data enable predictions in network biology with limited data?

provenance.text_excerpt: Fine-tuning towards a diverse panel of downstream tasks relevant to chromatin and network dynamics using limited task-specific data demonstrated that Geneformer consistently boosted predictive accuracy.

claims.statement: Geneformer, pretrained on Genecorpus-30M and fine-tuned with limited task-specific data, consistently improves predictive accuracy across diverse downstream tasks in network biology.

datasets.description: 29.9 million human single-cell transcriptomes from a broad range of tissues from publicly available data.
datasets.name: Genecorpus-30M

experiments_or_tasks: Architecture: 6-layer transformer encoder, input size 2048, 256 embedding dimensions, 4 attention heads, feed-forward size 512, ReLU activation, dropout 0.02, pretrained for 3 epochs with batch size 12, max learning rate 1e-3, linear warmup, Adam optimizer, weight decay 0.001.
Assembled Genecorpus-30M comprising 29.9 million human single-cell transcriptomes from diverse tissues.
Pretrained Geneformer using a self-supervised masked learning objective, masking 15% of genes per cell.

methods.name: Pretraining
methods.protocol_description: Self-supervised masked learning objective; masked 15% of genes; trained using cross-entropy loss.

methods.name: Fine-tuning
methods.protocol_description: Initialize with pretrained weights, add a task-specific transformer layer, fine-tune with max learning rate 5e-5, linear warmup, Adam weight decay fix, 500 warmup steps, weight decay 0.001, batch size 12, single epoch.

study_units.name: Geneformer pretraining and architecture

provenance.text_excerpt: Geneformer significantly boosted the ability to predict bivalently marked genes compared to alternative methods (AUC 0.93 and 0.88; bivalent versus unmethylated or H3K4me3-only, respectively)

results.value_raw_text: AUC 0.93 (bivalent versus unmethylated) and 0.88 (bivalent versus H3K4me3-only) for predicting bivalently marked genes in ESCs.

provenance.text_excerpt: Geneformer significantly boosted the ability to predict central versus peripheral factors compared to alternative methods (AUC 0.81)

results.value_raw_text: AUC 0.81 for distinguishing central versus peripheral factors in N1-dependent gene network using only normal endothelial cells without perturbation data.

provenance.text_excerpt: first, we fine-tuned Geneformer to distinguish cardiomyocytes35 from non-failing hearts (n=9) or hearts affected by hypertrophic (n=11) or dilated (n=9) cardiomyopathy with an overall out-of-sample accuracy of 90%

results.value_raw_text: Overall out-of-sample accuracy of 90% for distinguishing cardiomyocytes from non-failing, hypertrophic, or dilated cardiomyopathy hearts.

provenance.text_excerpt: in silico deletion of both GATA4 and TBX5 in combination had an even greater impact on their known cobound targets than the sum of their individual in silico deletion, suggesting that Geneformer recognized their cooperative action at these cobound targets.

claims.statement: In silico deletion of GATA4 and TBX5 in Geneformer captures cooperative effects on their cobound targets.

provenance.text_excerpt: CRISPR-mediated knockout of both Geneformer-predicted targets GSN and PLN in the TTN+/- cells significantly improved the contractile stress of the TTN+/- cardiac microtissues, validating these genes as promising candidate therapeutic targets for this disease.

claims.statement: Geneformer-predicted therapeutic targets GSN and PLN are validated as promising for dilated cardiomyopathy by experimental knockout improving contractile stress.

datasets.description: Single-cell transcriptomes from normal endothelial cells from the Heart Atlas (Litviňuková et al., Nature 2020).
datasets.name: Heart Atlas endothelial cells

experiments_or_tasks: Fine-tuned Geneformer to distinguish cardiomyocytes from non-failing, hypertrophic, or dilated cardiomyopathy hearts.
In silico deletion of GATA4 and TBX5 in fetal cardiomyocytes to model cooperative effects on target genes.
In silico treatment analysis: identified genes whose deletion shifts cardiomyocyte embeddings towards disease states, and genes whose inhibition shifts disease state embeddings towards non-failing.

methods.name: In silico deletion
methods.protocol_description: Remove a gene from the input rank value encoding and measure the change in cosine similarity of the cell embedding or gene embedding.

study_units.name: In silico perturbation and disease modelling

provenance.text_excerpt: CRISPR-mediated knockout of both Geneformer-predicted targets GSN and PLN in the TTN+/- cells significantly improved the contractile stress of the TTN+/- cardiac microtissues

results.value_raw_text: CRISPR-mediated knockout of GSN and PLN in TTN+/- cardiac microtissues significantly improved contractile stress.

provenance.text_excerpt: In silico deletion of GATA4 had a significantly higher effect on genes known to be most significantly dysregulated by GATA4 variants ... direct GATA4 targets ... were significantly more impacted by in silico deletion of GATA4 in fetal cardiomyocytes compared to indirect targets

results.value_raw_text: In silico deletion of GATA4 had significantly higher effect on direct targets than indirect targets or housekeeping genes (Wilcoxon, FDR-corrected).
